All key premises—specific microstructural evolution from annealing, phase stability, passive layer composition, and resulting corrosion performance—are presented without any reference to earlier experimental findings. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover these specific claims about APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi coatings on SS316L.
premises: APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L can be produced with a refined, dense structure by annealing at 550 °C
Annealing at 550 °C refines grain structure to ~15 µm with more low-angle boundaries and maintains a dominant BCC phase
The refined structure increases hardness and impedes dislocation motion
The coating rapidly forms stable Al- and Cr-rich passive oxide/hydroxide layers (e.g., Cr2O3, Fe(OH)3, Cr(OH)3, Co(OH)2) during corrosion
These combined effects enhance corrosion resistance (higher polarization resistance, lower hot-corrosion weight gain) relative to uncoated and as-sprayed SS316L
